claims.text: Substituting X with Al in CrFeCoNiX alloys promotes formation of a stable protective oxide layer above 900 °C.
The oxide promoted by Al is coherent and slow-growing.
Al selectively diffuses to the alloy surface during oxidation.
Surface Al reacts with oxygen to form an Al2O3 sublayer.
The Al2O3 sublayer is thin and adherent.
The Al2O3 sublayer relieves thermal and lattice-mismatch stresses.
CrFeCoNiX alloys with X = Si or Mn develop thicker and less coherent oxide scales than the Al-containing alloy.
Oxide scales on the Si- or Mn-containing variants are more prone to cracking and spallation.
A thin, continuous, adherent alumina-rich sublayer forms at the metal/oxide interface of the Al-containing alloy.
Selective oxidation of Al produces a slow-growing alumina scale.
Reduced lattice-mismatch and thermal stresses decrease cracking and spallation.
Under identical high-temperature exposure, the Al-containing alloy will have a thinner, more coherent, and more adherent oxide layer than the Si- and Mn-containing variants.
The oxide layer on the Al-containing alloy will remain intact under high-temperature oxidative conditions.
The proposed behavior applies above 900 °C to single- or multiphase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solutions in oxidative or corrosive environments.
Severe mechanical loads or significant secondary-phase precipitation may alter the proposed behavior.
Prior observations support Al selective oxidation and the resulting oxide coherence.
